APPENDIX ( Clause 3.3 )
DETERMINATION El. GENERAL OF FINENESS

B
OF DISPERSION

R-l.0 Fineness of dispersion is measured on a grind gauge?, consisting of a block of hardened steel into which has been machined a shallow groove varying in depth from zero at one end to 0.102 mm at the other. A sample of ink is placed at the deep end and is drawn down towards the shallow end by a steel scraper. Observation of any scratches in the ink film, and where they occur in terms of distance along the gauge, gives a measure of the degree of dispersion of the ink sample.
B-2. APPARATUS

- A hardened steel block approximately 180 mm in B-2.1 Gauget length, 63.5 mm in width and 12.5 mm in thickness. The top surface of the block shall be ground smooth and flat, and shall contain a groove 133.4 mm in length and 12.5 mm in width, centred in the top of the block. The groove shall be tapered uniformly in depth lengthwise from *Specification for petroleum hydrocarbon solvents ( second mision ). $Generaliy known as Hegman gauge. 6

IS:11259 0,102 mm at one end to zero depth at the other, calibrdted number in accordance with its depth as given in Table 1.

B-2.2 Scraper - A double-edged steel blade 87.5 mm long, wide and 6.8 mm thick. The two edges along the length rounded to a radius of approximately 0.25 mm. B-3. B-3.1 PROCEDURE This consists of the following steps: surface

37.5 mm shall be

4 b) cl

PJace the gauge on a flat, nonslippery immediately before the test.

and wipe it clean

Place the material to be tested in the deep end of the groove so that it overflows the groove slightly. Care shall be taken to see that the sample is free of air bubbles. Using both hands, hold the blade perpendicular to the block surface and at right angles to the length of the groove, draw the material down the length of the groove with a uniform deliberate motion. Use sufficient pressure to clean the level face of the gauge. 7

IS : 11259 - 1985 d) Immediately read the fineness as follows:

1) View the gauge from the side so that the line of vision is at right angles to the longer dimension of the groove. 2) Hold the gauge visible. in light that will make the pattern readily

3) For actual reading, make the angle between the face of the gauge and the line of vision not more than 30" nor less than 20". 4) Interpret the pattern and designate dispersion in microns or scale number, ignoring the few isolated and irregularly spaced particles towards the deep end of the groove. Using a fresh sample of the material each time, obtain three readings in the like manner. The first drawdown and reading is preliminary in order to establish proper conditions and to locate fineness pattern. With this known, the second and third readings can be made with a minimum time lapse between completion of drawdown and actual reading. No reading shall be considered for reporting fineness when the time lapse exceeds 10 seconds. B-3.2 Care of Gauge

4

The gauge shall be immediately cleaned after each reading. Use a solvent and a soft cioth. Keep the gauge covered at all times Gauges that lie idle for extended periods of when not in use. time shall be protected from rust. Do not allow any hard materials to come gauge surface or scraper in any manner Tapping or scratching scarring or nicking. surfaces shall be avoided. in contact with the that might result in with other metallic for !.tse by wear

4

may be rendered c) The scraper e of the contact dgeY edge or by warpage.

unsatisfactory

NOTE - Wear or warpage of the scraper may be noted by facing the edge of the scraper down on the smooth level face of the gauge and then inspecting the contact edge by means of a strong light, placed behind the gauge. Rocking the scraper forward or backward will reveal poor contact due to wear or warpage. If any face shows that the scraper has been damaged, it shall not be used.

APPENDIX ( Clause 3.5 )
DETERMINATION D-l. DEFINITION

D
DENSITY

OF RELATIVE

D-l.1 For the purpose of this standard, the relative density of the material is the ratio of the mass of a given volume of the material to that of an equal volume of distilled water, the temperature of both the material and the water being 27�C.
D-2.

shall be

Drawing, preparing, storing and handling of test samples, done in accordance with IS : 8883 ( Part 1 )-1978*. The sampling apparatus shall be clean and dry when used.

E-l.3 Precautions shall be taken to protect the samples, the material being sampled, the sampling apparatus and the containers for samples from adventitious contamination. E-l.5 The sample containers shall be of such a size that they completely filled by the sample.

E-1.6 Each sample container shall be sealed airtight with a stopper after filling, and marked with full details of sampling, the date of sampling and the month and year of manufacture of the material. E-3.

TEST SAMPLES

AND REFEREE SAMPLE

E-3.1 Preparation

of Test Samples

E-3.1.1 Take a small portion of the material from each container selected ( see Table 2 ), Thoroughly mix the material before drawing from the same container. Out of these portions, a small but equal quantity shall be taken for each selected container and shall be well mixed up together so as to form a composite sample of quantity sufficient to make triplicate determination for all the characteristics to be tested on the composite sample. This composite sample shal! be divided into three equal parts, one for the purchaser, another for the supplier and the third for the referee.
E-3.2

Referee Sample

shall consist of the composite sample E-3.2.1 Referee sample ( see E-3.1.1 ) and marked for the purpose and shall bear the seals of the purchaser and the supplier. This shall be kept at a place agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier and shall be used in case of a dispute between the two. E-4.
